notes: Adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game `binarytrees`, single-threaded reference shape (minDepth=4, stretch tree at maxDepth+1, long-lived tree at maxDepth, halving iteration counts). NOT the leaderboard entry: that one uses a bump arena (typed_arena) and rayon, which would measure an arena rather than the allocator/collector. Rust uses idiomatic Option<Box<Node>>, JS plain objects, Python a __slots__ class, VL a recursive struct `{left: Node | null, right: Node | null}`. Stdout is byte-identical across Rust/JS/VL at n=20 (verified with cmp). Scale-verified n=20 -> n=21 (2x work): rust 4.37->9.60s, deno 5.54->12.52s, VL 4.93->10.24s, python(16->17) 4.20->9.42s. Python's N is 16 (1/16 of the work). Final timings (min over all observations): rust 4.366s, deno 5.543s, VL 4.928s (prebuilt; 1.13x Rust and 0.89x deno — VL BEATS V8 here), python(16) 3.195s. `vl build -O3` is a wash (5.206s).
